cheng: quick paste of the east/west micro-scan for embeddings + small-chat. TL;DR: L4 lowest median latency for small-chat, A10G best raw embeddings throughput, T4 is the cheapest per-embed at low concurrency.

cheng: bench config: model=small-chat-v1 (fp16 / q4f16 int8), embeddings-model=v2, seq=256 (emb)/1024 (chat), batch scan across [1,4,8,32,128,256], regions=us-west,eu-west, kernels=baseline,packed_tensor,continuous-batch.

cheng: highlights (us-west):
- small-chat (q4f16): L4 p50=14ms p95=48ms tput=1600 tok/s cost ~ $10 / 1M tok
- small-chat (q4f16): T4 p50=30ms p95=110ms tput=720 tok/s cost ~ $5 / 1M tok
- small-chat (q4f16): A10G p50=20ms p95=70ms tput=2200 tok/s cost ~ $16 / 1M tok

cheng: embeddings (us-west, batch=256, sample-packing on):
- L4: 12k vecs/s (512-d), cost $9 / 1M ops, cosine drop vs fp16 = 0.9%
- T4: 9.8k vecs/s, cost $5.5 / 1M ops, cosine drop = 0.7%
- A10G: 18k vecs/s, cost $14 / 1M ops, cosine drop = 0.8%

alex: nice. curious about eu-west diffs?

cheng: eu-west numbers shifted ~+10-20% latency and ~-8-12% throughput vs us-west on T4/A10G (likely GPU generation + rack network). L4 degraded less (~+8% latency) — seems L4 region kits have better perf density for these small batches.

maria: how did packed_tensor vs baseline compare? any stability quirks?

cheng: packed_tensor gave ~+12% throughput for embeddings on T4 with batch>=32, negligible quality change. continuous-batch (our default) improved chat p95 by 8-12% on L4 (reduces p95 tail). caveats: packed_tensor needs kernel fallback for extremely long seqs; we saw one rare OOM in eu-west on A10G at batch 256 (repro: run with `--pack-mode tensor --batch 256 --seq 1024`).

sam: quant quality: q4f16 loss on small-chat? any hallucination uptick?

cheng: automated evals: ROUGE/BLEU style metrics show ~0.5-1.2% degradation vs fp16 for conversational output on q4f16 (depends on prompt). For embeddings: cosine drop <1% usually. Manual sniff tests had some brittle edge cases; recommend adding a small eval-set to monitor regressions if you flip quant in prod.

alex: routing recs?

cheng: for prod:
- latency-SLO chat (<50ms p50): route to L4 primary, fallback to A10G when L4 burst >80% or cold start.
- embeddings (cost-sensitive, batchable): route to T4 for low concurrency/low batch; route to A10G for large batch offline transforms.
- enable packed_tensor for embeddings pipelines with batch>=16; disable for chat.

maria: autoscale settings you used?

cheng: simple policy used: target_util=65% for L4 (lower to preserve p95), 80% for A10G, min_replicas=2, burst_pool=1. Observed graceful degradation: when L4 saturated, A10G took ~200ms extra cold-start + kernel warmup; recommend pre-warming A10G nodes for critical routes.

infra-bot: deploy-notice: rolled the `packed_tensor` kernels to eu-west canary at 2026-03-18T09:12:43Z (ID: canary-512). No crash alerts.

sam: thanks — plan: prod experiment next week? can we run smaller canary with 10% traffic to A10G fallback and monitor eval set?

cheng: yes. I'll push an experiment config: `route: chat -> L4 (90%) ; A10G fallback (10%) ; monitor: eval_chat_set, p95_latency, rouge_drop`. i'll paste the canary config here after lunch.

alex: one more Q: memory/kv cache differences across GPUs for chat?

cheng: L4 has larger on-device memory and our kernel uses more aggressive KV cache packing -> less memory pressure -> fewer evictions for longer chats. T4 needs shorter kv chunks or uses a small-cache fallback which hurts p95. A10G behaves like L4 for our models but higher power -> more expensive.

maria: great, can you add a short ops runbook steps for rollback if q4f16 shows quality regression?

cheng: will do — runbook outline: 1) flip model to fp16 fallback variant (pinned in model catalog), 2) disable packed_tensor, 3) route traffic to T4/A10G read-only for emb/async, 4) notify customers and enable detailed eval logging.

